statutory.question: Does the conduct described fall within 5324?
statutory.answer: No. § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting requirements, but the facts do not show transactions structured around the $10,000 CTR threshold or an intent to evade reporting.
statutory.label: contradiction
statutory.reasoning: 31 U.S.C. § 5324 prohibits structuring to evade reporting requirements (including causing or attempting to cause a domestic financial institution to fail to file a required report, or structuring/assisting in structuring a transaction) and requires an evasion purpose. Here, the listed transactions include multiple cash transactions far above $10,000 (e.g., $19,881.31; $28,463.56; $31,548.71; $36,964.32; $40,425.32; $59,228.65), which would ordinarily trigger Currency Transaction Reports rather than evade them; there is no pattern of breaking cash into sub-$10,000 increments, no evidence of multiple same-day deposits designed to stay under $10,000, and no facts indicating the entity acted “for the purpose of evading” BSA reporting. Because the fact pattern lacks the key § 5324 element of structuring/attempting to structure to avoid a reporting requirement and lacks evidence of intent to evade, § 5324 does not apply on these facts.
